section: Supreme Court - composition, appointment, collegium and NJAC, jurisdictions (original, appellate, advisory, writ)
subsections: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment

accepted.s: Under Article 124(2) of the Constitution, the President appoints a Judge of the Supreme Court after consulting the
o: Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
accepted.x: Article 124(2) requires consultation with the Chief Justice of India for appointment of a Supreme Court Judge. For appointments of other judges, consultation with the CJI is compulsory.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional authority specifically associated with the appointment power.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Judges Case, generally associated with S.P. Gupta, held that
o: consultation did not mean concurrence and executive primacy prevailed
consultation with the Chief Justice of India meant concurrence
the collegium consisted of the CJI and four senior-most judges
accepted.x: The First Judges Case, decided in 1981 and reported in 1982, held that consultation did not mean concurrence and recognised executive primacy in judicial appointments.
accepted.tq: Use the case-to-holding distinction to separate the three Judges Cases.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the ruling in the Second Judges Case of 1993?
o: It held that consultation means concurrence and gave primacy to the judiciary.
It struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment.
It upheld executive primacy in judicial appointments.
It expanded the collegium to the CJI and four senior-most judges.
accepted.x: The Second Judges Case held that consultation means concurrence, established judicial primacy and gave rise to the collegium consisting initially of the CJI and two senior-most judges.
accepted.tq: Match the landmark case with its distinctive constitutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The collegium was expanded to the Chief Justice of India and four senior-most Supreme Court judges by the
accepted.x: The Third Judges Case, arising from the Presidential Reference under Article 143 in 1998, expanded the Supreme Court collegium to the CJI and four senior-most judges.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related judicial decisions by the numerical composition they established.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Judges Cases:
1. The First Judges Case gave primacy to the executive.
2. The Second Judges Case created the collegium system.
3. The Third Judges Case reduced the collegium to the CJI and two senior-most judges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Third Judges Case expanded the collegium to the CJI and four senior-most judges.
accepted.tq: Find the altered numerical detail in the statement about the Third Judges Case.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Fourth Judges Case of 2015 is associated with which of the following outcomes?
o: Creation of the original collegium of three judges
Abolition of judicial primacy in appointments
Striking down of the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act, with restoration of the collegium
Validation of the NJAC Act and the 99th Amendment
accepted.x: In SCAORA v. Union of India, decided in 2015, the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act and restored the collegium system.
accepted.tq: Use the outcome of the case rather than its title to identify the correct option.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the collegium system, consider the following statements:
1. It is expressly mentioned in the Constitution of India.
2. It is a judicial creation arising from the Three Judges Cases.
3. It has been in its present form since 1998.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is false because the collegium has no express mention in the Constitution or in any constitutional amendment.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between a constitutional provision and a judicially evolved mechanism.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the High Court collegium?
o: The Union Law Minister and two eminent persons
The Chief Justice of India and four senior-most Supreme Court judges
The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court and two senior-most judges of that High Court
The Governor and two senior-most judges of the concerned High Court
accepted.x: The High Court collegium consists of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court and its two senior-most judges. Proposals for High Court appointments are initiated by the High Court Chief Justice.
accepted.tq: Separate the composition of the High Court collegium from the Supreme Court collegium.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the role of the High Court Chief Justice in the collegium process?
o: The High Court Chief Justice initiates proposals for appointments to the High Court.
The High Court Chief Justice appoints Supreme Court judges.
The High Court Chief Justice selects the two eminent persons in the NJAC.
The High Court Chief Justice ratifies the 99th Amendment.
accepted.x: Proposals for appointments to a High Court are initiated by the Chief Justice of that High Court through the High Court collegium.
accepted.tq: Ask who performs the initiating function rather than who formally appoints.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As of June 2026, which one of the following was NOT a member of the Supreme Court collegium?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court collegium in June 2026 comprised CJI Surya Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, B.V. Nagarathna, M.M. Sundresh and P.S. Narasimha. Justice J.K. Maheshwari had retired before that composition was reported.
accepted.tq: Use the current-membership list to identify the excluded name.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Justice B.R. Gavai was succeeded as Chief Justice of India by Justice Surya Kant after Justice Gavai's retirement in
accepted.x: Justice B.R. Gavai retired in November 2025 and was succeeded by Justice Surya Kant as Chief Justice of India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely placed dates in a recent constitutional appointment sequence.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was created through the
accepted.x: The NJAC was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014, along with the NJAC Act, 2014.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional body with the specific amendment that created it.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014 inserted which provision in the Constitution in connection with the NJAC?
accepted.x: The 99th Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 124A, among related provisions, to provide for the National Judicial Appointments Commission.
accepted.tq: Test the exact Article number associated with a constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NJAC Act, 2014 came into force on
accepted.x: The NJAC Act came into force on 13 April 2015. The date 31 December 2014 refers to Presidential assent to the 99th Amendment and the NJAC legislation.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates of assent, commencement and judicial invalidation.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the enactment of the NJAC framework:
1. The 99th Constitutional Amendment was passed by the Lok Sabha on 13 August 2014.
2. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 14 August 2014.
3. It received Presidential assent on 31 December 2014.
4. It was ratified by 16 States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the two Houses passed the measure on 13 and 14 August 2014, 16 States ratified it, and Presidential assent was given on 31 December 2014.
accepted.tq: Check each date and numerical detail independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a component of the six-member NJAC proposed under the 99th Amendment?
o: The two senior-most Supreme Court judges
accepted.x: The NJAC comprised the CJI as Chairperson, two senior-most Supreme Court judges, the Union Law Minister and two eminent persons. The Attorney-General of India was not a member.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority inserted into a specified constitutional composition.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proposal relating to representation of a person from the SC, ST, OBC, minority or women categories concerned the selection of
o: the two eminent persons in the NJAC
the two senior-most Supreme Court judges
accepted.x: One of the two eminent persons in the proposed NJAC was to be selected from among persons belonging to SC, ST, OBC, minority or women categories.
accepted.tq: Link a qualification condition to the correct component of a constitutional body.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Venkatachaliah Commission, which recommended the establishment of an NJAC, was appointed in 2000 under the Prime Ministership of
accepted.x: The Venkatachaliah Commission was appointed in 2000 during the Prime Ministership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and recommended an NJAC.
accepted.tq: Combine the commission's recommendation with its year and political context.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In SCAORA v. Union of India, the 2015 judgment striking down the NJAC was delivered by a five-judge Bench led by
accepted.x: The five-judge Bench in the Fourth Judges Case was led by Justice J.S. Khehar and struck down the NJAC and the 99th Amendment by a 4:1 majority.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the presiding judge from the lone dissenting judge in the same case.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the lone judge to dissent from the decision striking down the NJAC?
accepted.x: Justice J. Chelameswar was the lone dissenter and upheld the NJAC, whereas the majority declared the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act unconstitutional.
accepted.tq: Use the majority-dissent distinction as the decisive clue in a case-based question.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Third Judges Case expands the collegium to five members
B. First Judges Case recognises executive primacy
C. Fourth Judges Case strikes down the NJAC
D. Second Judges Case establishes judicial primacy and the collegium
accepted.x: The correct sequence is First Judges Case (1981), Second Judges Case (1993), Third Judges Case (1998), and Fourth Judges Case (2015).
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest Judges Cases, then place the two intervening cases by year.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the functioning of the collegium:
1. The Government conducts Intelligence Bureau background checks on recommended candidates.
2. The Government may return a name once for reconsideration.
3. If the collegium reiterates the recommendation, the Government is bound to appoint the person.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Government conducts background checks, may return a recommendation once, but is bound to appoint the candidate if the collegium reiterates it.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of scrutiny, one-time reconsideration and binding reiteration.
accepted.sec: Appointment - collegium and Judges cases, NJAC, 99th Amendment, CJI appointment  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
A. First Judges Case
B. Second Judges Case
C. Third Judges Case
D. Fourth Judges Case

List-II (Principal development)
1. NJAC and 99th Amendment struck down
2. Executive primacy
3. Collegium expanded to CJI and four senior-most judges
4. Consultation interpreted as concurrence and judicial primacy established

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The First Judges Case established executive primacy; the Second equated consultation with concurrence; the Third expanded the collegium; and the Fourth struck down the NJAC framework.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of the First Judges Case and eliminate incompatible codes.
